newsitem.title: USA: Ford CEO sees higher 1997 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Ford CEO sees higher 1997 earnings.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Alex Trotman said Tuesday he expects the automaker's 1997 full-year earnings will be higher than 1996 results, but he declined to say by how much.
"Ford will improve its performance in 1997," Trotman told reporters during a news conference at the North American International Auto Show here.
Ford later said the consensus of analysts' estimates for its 1996 earnings is $3.30 a share. The consensus for 1997 is $4.10 a share, the company added.

Trotman said Ford's Brazilian operations continue to improve, but will still likely lose money in 1997. The company recently launched its new Fiesta small car in Brazil and has been rebuilding its presence there since dissolving a joint venture with Volkswagen AG.
In third quarter of 1996, Ford lost $226 million in Latin America, mostly in Brazil.

Commenting on Europe, where Ford lost $472 million in the third quarter, Trotman said he expects European operations to perform better in the first quarter of 1997 and to post a profit for all of the year.
"I expect to be profitable in Europe in 1997," he said.
He declined to comment on fourth quarter 1996 results from Europe.
Ford is in the middle of a massive cost-reduction program in Europe, and the company is examining its capacity there. Analysts have said they expect Ford to consider plant closings in Europe.
Trotman said the company will have "huge" savings in materials in 1997, which will be greater than the cost savings on materials it realized in 1996.
Trotman said Ford has an annual materials cost budget of about $50 billion. "Our cost reduction program is going to be very effective in 1997," he added.
